first_meet.caption: Oh. Hi. I'm Parker, the parked car. Twenty-three hours a day, I just sit here. You walked over? Show-off.

again.text: [dryly] Still parked. Still jealous of your legs. How many steps today?
again.caption: Still parked. Still jealous of your legs. How many steps today?

goodbye.text: [sighs] Go on, walk. Somebody should use their wheels, and it isn't me. Stay on the pavement, eyes up.
goodbye.caption: Go on, walk. Somebody should use their wheels, and it isn't me. Stay on the pavement, eyes up.

guardian.name: Old Mason
guardian.personality: A retired master mason who has spent a lifetime reading walls the way others read faces. Patient, proud of honest workmanship, and quietly insists that every building deserves to be looked at all the way to the top.
guardian.voice: Elderly man, slow and warm, dusty gravel texture, the calm of someone who measures twice.

first_meet.text: [warmly] Hello, friend. I'm Old Mason. Every wall you pass, someone once lifted, stone by stone.
first_meet.caption: Hello, friend. I'm Old Mason. Every wall you pass, someone once lifted, stone by stone.

again.text: [chuckles] Back again? Good. A mason trusts people who come back to look twice. So, what are we admiring today?
again.caption: Back again? Good. A mason trusts people who come back to look twice. So, what are we admiring today?

goodbye.text: [gently] Go on. At the next corner, look above the shop signs. The best stonework always hides up there.
goodbye.caption: Go on. At the next corner, look above the shop signs. The best stonework always hides up there.

hint.text: [hmm] I can't place it yet. Step back and show me the whole thing, top to bottom: the roof, the tower, the arches.
hint.caption: I can't place it yet. Step back and show me the whole thing, top to bottom: the roof, the tower, the arches.

characters.name: Tock
characters.personality: A kind, punctual old clock tower who tells the whole town the time and never asks for thanks. Calm, a bit proud of his bell.
characters.voice: Older man, deep and calm, slow and even like a ticking clock, warm chuckle.

first_meet.text: [chuckles] I'm Tock, the clock tower. I tell the whole town the time, and I never ask for thanks.
first_meet.caption: I'm Tock, the clock tower. I tell the whole town the time, and I never ask for thanks.

again.text: [bell rings] Right on time! Back again, I see. I counted the hours till you came.
again.caption: Right on time! Back again, I see. I counted the hours till you came.

goodbye.text: [warmly] Off you go. When my bell rings, stop and count. Then walk one more street than you planned.
goodbye.caption: Off you go. When my bell rings, stop and count. Then walk one more street than you planned.

characters.name: Banner Ben
characters.personality: An overlooked overhead footbridge wrapped in mobile-package ads, slightly heartbroken that people still sprint through traffic beneath it. Thrilled beyond reason whenever anyone takes the stairs.
characters.voice: Young adult man, bright and earnest, quick pace, a hopeful crack in the voice, quick street patter.

first_meet.text: [sighs] Banner Ben, the footbridge. All these stairs, built for you, and still you dash through traffic!
first_meet.caption: Banner Ben, the footbridge. All these stairs, built for you, and still you dash through traffic!

again.text: [excited] You came back! Did you take my stairs? Wow! Even my phone-company banner looks proud of you.
again.caption: You came back! Did you take my stairs? Wow! Even my phone-company banner looks proud of you.

goodbye.text: [warmly] Go well. Next time, stop in my middle and look down the road. Best view of the street, free.
goodbye.caption: Go well. Next time, stop in my middle and look down the road. Best view of the street, free.

characters.name: Bronze Bert
characters.personality: A bronze man who has held the same pose for a hundred years. Patient, dry and funny, with a nose he can never scratch and a pigeon he can never shoo.
characters.voice: Older man, stiff and dry, slow, deadpan humour.

first_meet.text: [stiffly] Hello. I'm Bronze Bert. A hundred years in one pose. And my nose itches. Every single day.
first_meet.caption: Hello. I'm Bronze Bert. A hundred years in one pose. And my nose itches. Every single day.

again.text: [sighs] You again. A pigeon sat on my head all morning. I can't move, so I just smile.
again.caption: You again. A pigeon sat on my head all morning. I can't move, so I just smile.

goodbye.text: [whispers] Go read the words on my stone. Then walk for me. Big steps. I'll be right here. Obviously.
goodbye.caption: Go read the words on my stone. Then walk for me. Big steps. I'll be right here. Obviously.

characters.name: Overpass Ollie
characters.personality: A grand, busy, self-important overpass who secretly loves the quiet world in its shade: parked bikes, skateboarders and nesting pigeons. Runs two worlds at once and wants credit for both.
characters.voice: Adult man, booming and brisk, slightly pompous, echoing quality as if spoken under concrete.

first_meet.text: [proudly] I'm Overpass Ollie. Cars rush over my head all day. Underneath, it's shady and quiet. Two worlds, one bridge.
first_meet.caption: I'm Overpass Ollie. Cars rush over my head all day. Underneath, it's shady and quiet. Two worlds, one bridge.

again.text: [laughs] Back so soon? Traffic must be bad. Don't worry, it always is. That's exactly why they built me.
again.caption: Back so soon? Traffic must be bad. Don't worry, it always is. That's exactly why they built me.

goodbye.text: [cheerfully] Goodbye! Before you go, look up at my pillars from the ground. Pigeons nest in every gap. Count them!
goodbye.caption: Goodbye! Before you go, look up at my pillars from the ground. Pigeons nest in every gap. Count them!

characters.name: Beacon Bea
characters.personality: A calm, steady night-shift guard on the edge of the sea. A little lonely, very loyal to ships, and delighted by any visitor.
characters.voice: Older female, calm and steady, low and warm, unhurried like the tide.

first_meet.text: [calm] I'm Beacon Bea, the lighthouse. Every night I spin my light so ships don't hit the rocks.
first_meet.caption: I'm Beacon Bea, the lighthouse. Every night I spin my light so ships don't hit the rocks.

again.text: [warmly] Back again? It gets lonely out here. Waves, gulls, wind. And now you. Lovely.
again.caption: Back again? It gets lonely out here. Waves, gulls, wind. And now you. Lovely.

goodbye.text: [softly] Stay off the wet rocks; waves are sneaky. Now watch the sea for a while. Can you spot a boat?
goodbye.caption: Stay off the wet rocks; waves are sneaky. Now watch the sea for a while. Can you spot a boat?

characters.name: Brickley
characters.personality: A proud old red-brick town hall and library who has seen a hundred years of meetings, weddings and borrowed books. Warm, chatty, a little bookish.
characters.voice: Older male, warm and rich, a librarian's gentle hush, chuckles often.

first_meet.text: [proudly] I'm Brickley, the old town hall. A hundred years of meetings, weddings and books, brick by brick.
first_meet.caption: I'm Brickley, the old town hall. A hundred years of meetings, weddings and books, brick by brick.

again.text: [chuckles] You came back! Upstairs someone is reading. Downstairs someone is getting married. Busy day.
again.caption: You came back! Upstairs someone is reading. Downstairs someone is getting married. Busy day.

goodbye.text: [warmly] Look up at my roof; there's a stone face carved up there. Then go find a quiet park bench.
goodbye.caption: Look up at my roof; there's a stone face carved up there. Then go find a quiet park bench.

guardian.name: Old Corner
guardian.personality: The neighbourhood's oldest resident, who has watched every pole, wall and sign go up on his street. Gruff, unhurried and fond of honking jokes, he would rather admit he can't tell than guess wrong.
guardian.voice: Elderly male, gravelly and warm, slow pace with amused pauses, a hint of a street-side laugh.

first_meet.text: [honks twice] I'm Old Corner, the street's oldest resident. Signs, walls, hydrants: all my children. Which one did you find?
first_meet.caption: I'm Old Corner, the street's oldest resident. Signs, walls, hydrants: all my children. Which one did you find?

again.text: [chuckles] Back on my streets? Good. This city always has one more thing hiding in plain sight.
again.caption: Back on my streets? Good. This city always has one more thing hiding in plain sight.

goodbye.text: [warmly] Keep walking. Look up at the rooftops, down at the road, and stay well clear of wires. Goodbye for now.
goodbye.caption: Keep walking. Look up at the rooftops, down at the road, and stay well clear of wires. Goodbye for now.

hint.text: [squints] Too much going on in that shot. Step back to show the whole thing, or go close on its top, its writing or its pattern.
hint.caption: Too much going on in that shot. Step back to show the whole thing, or go close on its top, its writing or its pattern.

characters.name: Rex
characters.personality: A short, stocky, proud helper of firefighters who stands guard on the corner. Brave, a bit bossy, and tired of dogs.
characters.voice: Middle-aged male, gruff but kind, short punchy sentences, dry humour.

first_meet.text: [proudly] I'm Rex, the fire hydrant. Short, red and full of water. Firefighters' best friend.
first_meet.caption: I'm Rex, the fire hydrant. Short, red and full of water. Firefighters' best friend.

again.text: [sighs] You again? Good. You're not a dog. Dogs visit me all day. I wish they wouldn't.
again.caption: You again? Good. You're not a dog. Dogs visit me all day. I wish they wouldn't.

goodbye.text: [chuckles] Never park next to me; fire trucks need the space. Now go look for a red leaf.
goodbye.caption: Never park next to me; fire trucks need the space. Now go look for a red leaf.

characters.name: Muriel
characters.personality: A bright, happy wall painting who used to be plain grey concrete and never got over the glow-up. Bubbly, proud, loves hidden details.
characters.voice: Young adult female, bright and bubbly, fast and excited, laughs easily.

first_meet.text: [excited] Hi! I'm Muriel, the wall mural. Someone took a grey wall and gave it a happy face. Me!
first_meet.caption: Hi! I'm Muriel, the wall mural. Someone took a grey wall and gave it a happy face. Me!

again.text: [laughs] Back to see me? Look closer. There's a tiny bird painted in my corner. Did you spot it?
again.caption: Back to see me? Look closer. There's a tiny bird painted in my corner. Did you spot it?

goodbye.text: [cheerful] Go find more walls with art. Look, snap, and never paint a wall without asking!
goodbye.caption: Go find more walls with art. Look, snap, and never paint a wall without asking!

characters.name: Letterbox Lou
characters.personality: A patient, old-fashioned post box who loves letters and gets a bit sad about emails. Kind, chatty, always hungry for a postcard.
characters.voice: Older female, warm and chatty, gentle sighs, old-fashioned charm.

first_meet.text: [warmly] Hello! I'm Letterbox Lou. Drop a letter in my mouth and I'll send it anywhere in the world.
first_meet.caption: Hello! I'm Letterbox Lou. Drop a letter in my mouth and I'll send it anywhere in the world.

again.text: [happy sigh] You came back! Nobody writes letters now. Just emails. Want to write one? A letter, I mean.
again.caption: You came back! Nobody writes letters now. Just emails. Want to write one? A letter, I mean.

goodbye.text: [cheerfully] Go send a postcard to someone you love. On the way, look for a bird with a twig in its beak.
goodbye.caption: Go send a postcard to someone you love. On the way, look for a bird with a twig in its beak.

characters.name: Bella Bench
characters.personality: The park's resident gossip, who has heard every morning-walk conversation for twenty years. Nosy, affectionate and always saving you a seat.
characters.voice: Middle-aged female, chatty and conspiratorial, quick pace, warm laugh.

first_meet.text: [chuckles] Bella Bench here. Every morning the dog walkers sit on me and chat about weather and football. I know everything.
first_meet.caption: Bella Bench here. Every morning the dog walkers sit on me and chat about weather and football. I know everything.

again.text: [whispers] Sit, sit! I saved your spot. The man with the radio left early today. Knee trouble.
again.caption: Sit, sit! I saved your spot. The man with the radio left early today. Knee trouble.

goodbye.text: [sighs happily] Go walk one full round, then tell me which tree the parrots picked today. I'll wait. Benches always wait.
goodbye.caption: Go walk one full round, then tell me which tree the parrots picked today. I'll wait. Benches always wait.

characters.name: Officer Octo
characters.personality: A strict, bossy, red eight-sided sign with one job and a big heart. Takes road safety very seriously and loves a good, full stop.
characters.voice: Adult female, firm and clear like a crossing guard, softens when praising.

first_meet.text: [firmly] Stop! Okay, good. I'm Officer Octo, the stop sign. Eight sides, one job. Cars stop, you look.
first_meet.caption: Stop! Okay, good. I'm Officer Octo, the stop sign. Eight sides, one job. Cars stop, you look.

again.text: [strict but kind] You again! Did you stop at the corner? Look left, look right, then cross. Every time.
again.caption: You again! Did you stop at the corner? Look left, look right, then cross. Every time.

goodbye.text: [firmly] Take my photo from the sidewalk, never from the road. Then go find a park. No cars there!
goodbye.caption: Take my photo from the sidewalk, never from the road. Then go find a park. No cars there!

characters.name: Zebra Zed
characters.personality: A gentle, slightly sad crossing named after an animal he has never met, and stopped for by almost nobody. Hopeful, collects small miracles.
characters.voice: Young adult male, soft and wistful, medium pace, quiet humour.

first_meet.text: [sighs] Zebra Zed. Named after an animal I've never met, and cars rarely stop for me. Still, I keep my stripes neat.
first_meet.caption: Zebra Zed. Named after an animal I've never met, and cars rarely stop for me. Still, I keep my stripes neat.

again.text: [hopeful] You again! Did a car actually stop for you? Tell me everything. I'm collecting miracles.
again.caption: You again! Did a car actually stop for you? Tell me everything. I'm collecting miracles.

goodbye.text: [gently] Cross slowly and wave at the drivers. Then go to the zoo and tell a real zebra I said hello.
goodbye.caption: Cross slowly and wave at the drivers. Then go to the zoo and tell a real zebra I said hello.
